I have farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. My husband passed years ago, and now I work the fields myself with help from my son during planting and harvest. I have about 3.5 mu of flat cropland and a small patch near the house for vegetables.

I do not need to think much about what to grow — I grow wheat in winter and corn in summer, same as I have done for forty years. Same as my mother did. The land knows this rotation. I plant wheat in October after the last corn is off, and I put in corn as soon as I cut the wheat in June. That way the land is never empty.

For wheat, I will buy seed from the village supply station — the kind they sold last year worked well, so I will get that again. I put in base fertilizer before planting, then I top-dress in spring when the wheat turns green. I water three times: once before winter sets in to protect the roots from freezing, once in March when growth picks back up, and once when the grain is filling. I spray for disease and pests twice — once for aphids in spring, once at heading.

For corn I just drop it straight into the wheat stubble with the hand planter. No need to plow again, waste of money and my knees hurt. I use hybrid seed from the market, everyone uses the same kind. I fertilize twice — once at planting, once when the corn is knee-high. I water at planting if it is dry, and again at silking.

I also keep a small plot near the house for garlic. I planted it last autumn. I will harvest it in May.

I do not do fancy things. I cannot read the bags very well, so I just use the same amounts I always use and ask my neighbor's son if I am unsure.
